title: Cullera 500: Back Where European Footvolley Began
text:
The Mediterranean Footvolley Cup brought the League of Champions to a very special place in the history of the sport: Playa de San Antonio in Cullera.

It was here in 1993 that the first footvolley competition in Europe was held. More than three decades later, European footvolley returned to the same beach for another weekend of top-level competition.

Facu SILVA & JOEL CORTES WINS THE 500

In the 500 tournament, Facu Silva and Joel Cortes took the title after a thrilling 2–1 victory in the final, making the win even sweeter for Joel on his home beach. Daine Morris and Lukki came incredibly close to the title, with Daine reaching his first League of Champions final.

Iaco and Miquel joined forces at the last minute and still managed to claim third place, while Robert and Jona from Alicante produced one of the surprises of the weekend by reaching the top four.

Guillem & Charly Take the 100

In the 100 tournament, Guillem Torres and Charly proved to be a rock-solid partnership, using their defensive strength to go all the way and claim the title.

Marco de Mello from BCN and Luisinho reached the final in their very first tournament together, while old-school player Edu Baquero and Kevin from Karlsruhe turned another last-minute partnership into a third-place finish.

Vini Silva and Keyvan completed the top four after another surprise run.

From the first European tournament in 1993 to the Mediterranean Footvolley Cup today, Playa de San Antonio continues to be part of the story of European footvolley.

title: Otero & Silva Crowned Matosinhos 1000 Champions and Cement No. 1 Ranking
text:
AirDesigners had promised a major footvolley celebration in Matosinhos, Portugal — and the final 1000 tournament of the 2026 season delivered.

At the top of the podium were Rodrigo Otero and Juan Silva, who claimed their first 1000 title together. After an incredibly consistent season across Europe, the victory further cemented their position as No. 1 in the international League of Champions ranking.

The runners-up were Beto Correia and Kleyber Xavier Silva from C.D. Santaluziense, who produced an impressive run on home soil.

Another breakthrough came from Jakob and Klemens Hofmann-Wellenhof, with the brothers reaching their first-ever semifinal at a 1000 tournament. Their run eventually ended against Hertha BSC's Joel Nisslein and Mitch Weber, who secured a place on the podium.

Yosy & Antonia Take the Women's Title

The women's tournament brought together two of Europe's biggest names, as Yosy Silva and Antonia Missethan joined forces in Matosinhos. The new partnership lived up to expectations, taking the title ahead of Mariana Felisberto and Clara Bezerra from CT Alan Cavalcanti.

The victory also puts Yosy Silva at No. 1 in the women's ranking with 3,800 points, followed by Antonia Missethan with 2,800 points.

With the final 1000 event completed, attention is increasingly turning towards the League of Champions Finals in Faro. And it is not only the individual rankings worth watching: the club ranking will determine the qualification quota for the Finals, making every result across the season count.

Matosinhos was another reminder of how quickly European footvolley is developing — and now, the race to Faro is on.

title: Copenhagen 1000 Becomes a New Flagship of European Footvolley
text:
Copenhagen 1000 delivered a historic weekend for European footvolley, transforming Kongens Nytorv in the heart of Copenhagen into a spectacular arena for three days of world-class action.

An estimated 50,000+ people passed by the stadium during the event, experiencing footvolley up close in the middle of the Danish capital. The level on the court matched the setting. European footvolley is stepping up — stronger players, stronger clubs, bigger events and a sport that is visibly growing across the continent.

The men's title went to SS Lazio, with Federico Iacopucci and Anderson Aguia taking the Copenhagen 1000 crown. Juan Silva and Rodrigo Otero, representing Politécnico do Porto, finished runners-up after another deep run in what has already been an outstanding 2026 season.

One of the biggest surprises came from CSV Frankenthal. Michael Weber and Robin Orschel secured third place after defeating the strong Hertha BSC partnership of Lukas Kicherer and Joel Nisslein.

In the women's tournament, Yosy Silva and her Brazilian partner Anna Mendes, representing Serfay, took the title and completed an incredible weekend of footvolley in Copenhagen.

50,000+ people. World-class footvolley. Right in the heart of the city.

Copenhagen 1000 showed just how far European footvolley has come — and where it might be heading next.

title: Juan Silva & Otero Lead 2026  Ranking After Santa Luzia 500
text:
The League of Champions returned to Portugal for the Santa Luzia 500, bringing together many of the country's top players for another exciting stop on the 2026 tour.

In the men's competition, Juan Silva and Rodrigo Otero continued their outstanding season by capturing yet another League of Champions title. The duo showcased the consistency that has made them Europe's leading duo and put Politecnico do Porto as leaders of the men’s club competition, defeating Alejandro Faurlin and Artura Bernal in the final to claim the 500 ranking points. Kleyber and Lucas Pinheiro completed the podium after an impressive tournament, while Daniel Duarte and Nivaldo Barros also enjoyed a strong run to the semifinals.

The women's tournament saw a memorable triumph for the home crowd as Isabella Serafim and Luisa Gateira of Santaluziense claimed the title in front of their local supporters. Bruna Gomes and Lele Lungano, representing CT Alan Cavalcanti, finished as runners-up, while Anna Mendes secured third place.

With passionate fans, outstanding local organization and another weekend of top-class competition, Santa Luzia once again demonstrated why Portugal remains one of Europe's true footvolley powerhouses. As the race for the League of Champions Finals intensifies, every ranking point is becoming increasingly valuable.

title: London 100 Makes Footvolley History in the UK 🇬🇧🏆
text:
The London 100 marked a historic milestone as the first international footvolley tournament ever held in the United Kingdom. Hosted by SideOut Footvolley, the event welcomed players from across the UK alongside visitors from Portugal, France and Sweden, proving that British footvolley is ready to take its place on the European stage.

The men's title was claimed by the exciting young duo Lucas "LC" Rodrigues and Fellype Lopes, representing Swindon Footvolley. Still only 18 years old, LC announced himself as one of Britain's brightest emerging talents, while the pair showed remarkable composure to win a thrilling three-set final against Portugal's Zé Moura and João Moreira.

Swindon Footvolley enjoyed an outstanding weekend, with founder João Paulo de Oliveira ("JP") also reaching the podium alongside Raphael Oliveira, while another Swindon partnership, Icaro Da Rosa and Nicolas Campanha, impressed by reaching the semifinals in their very first tournament together.

The women's competition produced another memorable final. Nathielly Antunes of SideOut Footvolley joined forces with Amanda Sardeli from Birmingham Footvolley, combining youth and experience to capture the title after a hard-fought three-set victory over Raiane Souza and Natalia Moura of the newly established Loughborough Footvolley.

Beyond the results, London 100 highlighted the rapid growth of the women's game in Britain, with players from SideOut, Birmingham, Loughborough and Swindon all reaching the latter stages of the tournament.

Perhaps the biggest success of the weekend was not a trophy, but what it represented. Talented young players, experienced competitors and passionate club builders came together to create an event that felt both highly competitive and incredibly welcoming.

With two thrilling finals, international participation and an enthusiastic local community, London has officially joined the European footvolley map.

If this was the first chapter, the future of British footvolley looks exceptionally bright. 🇬🇧🌍

title: Recap: Elite Cup 1000. Saint Laurent du Var 1000. Nordic Footvolley 100. One Growing European Tour. 🌍🏆
text:
It has been another unforgettable chapter in the League of Champions season, with three tournaments across Europe showcasing the incredible growth of the sport. From record-breaking fields in Italy to spectacular venues in France and the unique community spirit of the Nordics, footvolley continues to reach new heights.

Elite Cup 1000 – Cervia 🇮🇹

The Elite Cup 1000 made history, attracting a record 53 men's teams and 12 women's teams, making it one of the biggest international footvolley tournaments ever held.

The title went to Ron Ben Ishai and Maor Haas proving once again that they belong among the world's elite.

Another major highlight of the weekend was the annual Ballon d'Or of Footvolley, where Federico Iacopucci of Lazio Footvolley received the prestigious award after one of the closest votes in recent memory.

Hertha BSC also impressed. Lukas Kicherer and Joel Nisslein finished runners-up after an outstanding weekend. Afterwards, Joel described it as "our best tournament so far"—a strong statement from one of Europe's most consistent teams.

In the women's competition, Antonia Missethan and Julia Sauer-Rauch continued their dominant season, adding another Elite Cup title to their growing list of achievements.

Saint Laurent du Var 1000 🇫🇷

The tour then moved to the French Riviera, where Saint Laurent du Var 1000 delivered world-class footvolley in spectacular surroundings.

With incredible sports facilities and a packed stadium creating an electric atmosphere, the event quickly became one of the highlights of the season.

The winners were Facu Silva and Joel Cortes, representing Serfay, who produced outstanding footvolley throughout the weekend.

Finishing second were one of the season's most exciting new duplas: Mark "Haalandinho" Thom, who has joined forces with Brazilian star Vina. The new partnership continues to improve with every tournament and looks increasingly dangerous heading into the second half of the season.

The women's title once again belonged to Antonia Missethan and Julia Sauer-Rauch, who backed up their Cervia victory with another outstanding performance.

Nordic Footvolley 100 – Helsinki 🇫🇮

Further north, the Nordic Footvolley 100 brought together the Scandinavian community for its third edition in Helsinki.

More than just a tournament, the Nordic stop has become a celebration of the region's growing footvolley family. Players from across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark gathered for a fantastic day filled with competition, friendship and shared passion for the sport.

Home favourites Belinho and Jean Silva, representing Helsinki Footvolley, claimed the title after an impressive performance.

Last year's champions, Rufus and Daniel Bessa, once again reached the final and finished as runners-up, underlining their consistency at the Nordic event.

In the women's competition, Carin Nylander and Ana Clara captured the Nordic title, completing a fantastic weekend in Helsinki.

Three tournaments.

Three countries.

One united European footvolley community.

From record-breaking events to family gatherings on Nordic sand, the League of Champions continues to prove that European footvolley is growing faster than ever. With every stop, the level rises, new stories are written, and the community becomes stronger.

The season rolls on. 🌍🏆

title: Elite Cup 1000 Set to Break Records in Cervia 🔥
text:
The wait is almost over.

This weekend, the Elite Cup 1000 arrives in Cervia, and might be the biggest international footvolley tournament ever assembled?

A staggering 53 men's teams and 12 women's teams have signed up, creating one of the deepest and most competitive fields European footvolley has ever seen. From title contenders and Brazilian professionals to rising talents and local heroes, Cervia will become the center of the footvolley world.

At the top of the men's field, all eyes will be on the current League leaders Rodrigo Otero and Juan Silva. The Portuguese-Brazilian partnership has set the standard throughout the season and arrives as the team everyone wants to beat.

But the challengers are everywhere.

The battle for the podium becomes even more intense with Joel Nislein and Lukas Kicherer representing Hertha Berlin. Joel remains one of the most consistent players in Europe, and Hertha always seems to be in contention when the trophies are handed out.

Fresh off their Graz 1000 victory, Ron ben Ishai and Maor Haas have climbed to second in the rankings.

Then there is perhaps the comeback story of the season. Michael Weber and Dennis Weber have fought their way back into the elite after Michael's long injury layoff. Sitting fifth in the rankings, nobody doubts their talent. The only question is whether Cervia will be the weekend they fully announce themselves as top contenders?

Italy's hopes rest heavily on Federico Iacopucci and Ludovico Alonzi. After their breakthrough League of Champions victory earlier this season, the Lazio stars have become one of the most feared duplas on tour. Playing on “home sand” only adds to the excitement.

When you mix fire with gasoline, you get Alain Faccini and Tadeo Gooley. Their performances in Graz showcased everyone they belong among Europe's elite.

The women's tournament is equally exciting.

League leaders Antonia Missethan and Julia Sauer-Rauch arrive with a commanding lead in the rankings, but challengers such as Yosy Silva and Laura Martinez, along with Nina Steinbauer and Julia Jonasson, are ready to fight for one of the most prestigious titles of the season. Yosy Silva not teaming up with her regular partner Keyla Faria who is injured.

During the weekend, the annual Ballon d'Or of Footvolley will be awarded. Insiders say the voting has been closer than ever before, reflecting a season filled with new champions, breakthrough performances, and fierce rivalries. For the first time in years, there is no obvious winner.

One thing is certain:

The biggest names.
The biggest field.
The closest Ballon d'Or race ever.

Everything points towards a historic weekend in Cervia. And for fans around the world, every match will be streamed live on Bolao.TV.

The stage is set. 🍿🏆🌍🔥

title: The Race for the League of Champions Title Heats Up After Graz 1000 🏆🌍
text:
The dust has settled after an unforgettable Graz 1000, and for the first time this season, the League standings are beginning to tell a real story. With major points awarded and new contenders emerging, the battle for the 2026 title is shaping up to be the most competitive in League history.

At the top sits Juan Silva with 1,400 points. The Brazilian living in Portugal has been the definition of consistency this season, reaching deep stages of every major tournament while collecting victories and podiums. With his win in Stockholm 100 he’s just 100 points ahead of his dupla Rodrigo Otero.

As mentioned, close behind is Rodrigo Otero on 1,300 points. Since joining forces with Silva, the duo has become one of the most feared teams in Europe. They have already collected major titles and podium finishes, and despite losing the Graz 1000 final, they remain firmly in the championship conversation.

The biggest movers after Graz are Ron ben Ishai and Maor Haas. Their victory in Graz immediately launches them to third place overall with 1,000 points each. They entered the season later than most, but if they continue to play the major events, they suddenly become serious contenders for the overall title.

Just behind them are the Italian stars Ludovico Alonzi and Federico Iacopucci, whose breakthrough victory in Vilanova proved they belong among Europe's elite. The Lazio duo currently occupy fifth place and continue to build momentum.

One player who keeps proving his class is Joel Nislein. Last season's number one sits seventh overall and continues to produce strong results regardless of partner. While he may not have collected a major title yet in 2026, few players are as consistently dangerous as the Hertha Berlin star.

The comeback story of the season belongs to the Weber brothers. Dennis Weber and Michael Weber share eighth place with 540 points each after Michael's return from a long knee injury. The brothers have already shown flashes of their best form, and many now see them as genuine threats at every major tournament on the calendar.

Meanwhile, Isli Bejtaga has quietly built one of the most impressive seasons on tour. Sitting tenth overall, he has established himself as one of the strongest all-around competitors in Europe. His performances in Graz, including victories over the Lazio stars, confirmed that he belongs among the continent's elite. If Team Isli can convert deep runs into tournament wins, he could climb rapidly up the standings.

Another name worth watching is Nerynho Schaitl. Currently 18th in the rankings, the Amsterdam player has shown glimpses of brilliance throughout the season. While the results have not yet matched the very top contenders, his trajectory suggests that bigger breakthroughs could be just around the corner.

And perhaps that is the story of 2026 so far: uncertainty. New tournament winners, new partnerships, returning legends, and rising talents have created a season where nobody has been able to take full control.

With several major stops still to come — including Matosinhos 1000, Aveiro 500, Valencia 500, and the yet-to-be-announced Finals — the race is far from over.

The rankings are taking shape.

And the fight for the League of Champions crown is wide open. 🏆🌍🔥

title: Graz 1000 Delivers an incredible show
text:
Ron & Maor won, but was Isli the big surprise?

The Graz 1000 lived up to every expectation and more. With 113 games teams over the weekend, a packed city-center venue at Freiheitsplatz, and an additional 100-category tournament running alongside it, Graz became the beating heart of European footvolley for an unforgettable weekend.

The level was extraordinary. Europe's best teams faced Brazilian professionals in match after match, showcasing just how far the sport has come. The event once again highlighted what the League of Champions is all about: bringing together the very best players in Europe while creating opportunities for the next generation of talents to rise.

One of the standout stories came from Isli, who further cemented himself as one of Europe's elite players. Together with his partner Anderson Aguia, he defeated SS Lazio Footvolley stars Ludovico Alonzi and Federico Iacopucci twice during the tournament. Although Team Isli ultimately finished in 4th place, their performances left no doubt that they belong among the strongest duplas in Europe.

Another fan-favorite storyline was the return of Alain Faccini, one of the true icons of European footvolley. Partnering with Tadeo, who flew in directly from Brazil, Faccini showed flashes of the level that made him one of the continent's most respected players.

Meanwhile, every team that did not qualify for the main draw had the chance to compete in the parallel 100 tournament, creating another stage for emerging players. Here, FTV Bergen produced one of the surprises of the weekend, storming all the way to the final. Their rapid development is a testament to the growth of Norwegian footvolley.

In the end, however, the title went to Footvolley Zurich, with Caio and Felix claiming their first-ever League of Champions victory and their first 100 ranking points. A milestone achievement for the Swiss duo.

In the main 1000 tournament, the title was secured by Ron and Maor, who defeated Juan Silva and Rodrigo Otero in the final. Given their pedigree and recent form, it was a result few would consider surprising.

If Graz proved anything, it is that European footvolley has never been deeper. New talents are rising, established stars continue to evolve, and every tournament seems to produce a new storyline.

The season rolls on. The level keeps rising. And the race for the League of Champions title is wide open. 🌍🏆

title: A Massive Weekend Awaits. 113 games in graz 1000🔥

title: Joel and Lukki Takes First Win of This Season In Kalogria
text:
The Kalogria 100 delivered a unique mix of elite competition, training, and Mediterranean atmosphere as players from across Europe gathered on one of Greece’s most stunning beaches.

The tournament was won by Lukas Kicherer and Joel Nislein, representing Hertha Berlin. The duo showed strong chemistry and control throughout the event, securing an important victory in Greece.

Second place went to Rufus Wiena and Pedro Miranda, representing both FTV Athens and Hertha Berlin — a format unique to 100-category tournaments, where duplas can represent two different clubs. With another strong result, Pedro Miranda now climbs to an overall 8th place in the League standings.

Third place was claimed by Alex and Lutz from FTV Club Graz.

Beyond the matches, Kalogria became much more than just a tournament stop. The event combined a full training retreat with an official League of Champions European Open, marking an important moment for Greece’s return to the international footvolley stage.

The days leading up to the competition featured organized training sessions, open play, and long hours on the sand, giving players the opportunity to prepare, improve, and connect. Throughout the week, the atmosphere highlighted the growing strength of the European footvolley community, bringing together players, ideas, coaches, organizers, and new faces from across the continent.

With beautiful surroundings, strong competition, and a relaxed but passionate energy, Kalogria 100 once again showed how footvolley continues to grow through both competition and community.

title: Full 2026 League of Champions Calendar Released – Biggest Season Ever 🌍🔥
text:
*Matosinhos is a 1000 tournament!

The full calendar for the League of Champions 2026 season has now been officially announced — and it marks a historic step forward for European footvolley.

With 18 stops across the continent, this is the largest and most ambitious season ever. New locations are entering the map, expanding both reach and energy: Nordic Footvolley 100 in Helsinki, London 100, Matosinhos 1000, Aveiro 500, and Valencia 500 all join the journey.

From Scandinavia to Southern Europe, from emerging communities to established powerhouses, the League continues to grow — not just in size, but in level, diversity, and connection.

The Finals location is still to be revealed, adding another layer of anticipation to an already explosive season.

And the competition? It’s already heating up. With new tournament winners emerging early in the season, the race for the title is more open than ever. There is no clear favorite — only momentum, form, and who can deliver when it matters most.

The growth is here.
The international community is here.

Strap in — 2026 is going to be something special.

title: LAZIO TAKES FIRST EVER GOLD IN VILANOVA 500
text:
Male winners Vilanova 500

The Vilanona 500 delivered a spectacular weekend of footvolley, as Europe’s best teams gathered in perfect conditions on the Catalan coast.

Hosted by BCN Footvolley, one of the largest and most vibrant footvolley communities in Europe, the event combined elite competition with an electric beach atmosphere. With sunshine, packed courts, and a constant flow of high-level matches, Vilanova became the center of European footvolley.

The tournament victory went to Lazio Footvolley, with Federico Iacopucci and Ludovico Alonzi claiming their first-ever League of Champions title. Their level throughout the tournament was exceptional — composed, explosive, and fearless. For this Italian dupla, it feels like only the beginning.

Second place went to the Portuguese surprise team CT Alan Cavalcanti, with João Alcantra and Carlos Eduardo Paulino dos Santos. Starting all the way from Friday qualifications, they played beautifully technical footvolley all weekend and fought their way into the final — one of the standout stories of the event.

Third place once again went to Politécnico do Porto, with Juan Silva and Rodrigo Otero, continuing their strong and consistent 2026 season.

Just behind them, Dennis Weber and Michael Weber confirmed their return to top-level competition with another top 4 finish.

The women’s tournament delivered one of the highlights of the weekend. In a thrilling final, Antonia Missethan and Julia Rauch, representing BCN Footvolley, faced off against Yosy Silva and Kayla Faria from Serfay. In front of an energized crowd, the Barcelona duo secured the win in an amazing comeback and a match that showcased the growing level of the women’s game.

With incredible matches, perfect weather, and a powerful local community behind it, Vilanova 500 showed exactly what European footvolley is becoming.

The level is rising.
The stories are growing.

And Europe is watching.

title: Silva & Otero Take the Crown at Amsterdam 500 🏆
text:
Male winners Amsterdam 500

The Amsterdam 500 delivered an intense weekend of indoor footvolley, with more than 20 teams gathering in the Dutch capital for the strongest event of the season so far.

Taking the title — and the full 500 League points — were Juan Silva and Rodrigo Otero. Last season’s number six and seven are a dupla everyone is watching for this season. Representing Politécnico do Porto, the pair played a composed and powerful tournament, establishing themselves as one of the teams to beat this year.

A big storyline of the tournament was the return of Michael Weber, who teamed up again with his brother Dennis Weber after a long knee injury. The brothers looked strong throughout the event, raising an exciting question for the rest of the season: could the Weber brothers become title contenders at every major tournament this year?

Third place went to Hertha Berlin, with Joel Nisslein — last season’s number one — this time partnering with Pedro Miranda.

One of the biggest surprises came from the young Swiss duo Louis Weckerle and Lenny Quintas from Basel footvolley, who finished an impressive 4th place. Their performance showed that the future of European footvolley is looking bright.

With Amsterdam Footvolley hosting a strong and well-organized event, the season continues to gain momentum.

Next stop: Barcelona 500 in Vilanova just outside Barcelona.

See you on the sand.

title: Footvolley in surreal sorroundings? Mandal 100 Joins League of Champions
text:
Footvolley in Mandal 2025

The League of Champions continues its European journey north as Mandal 100 officially enters the calendar.

Set on the spectacular southern coastline of Mandal, this new stop brings the League to one of Scandinavia’s most breathtaking beaches. White sand, open sea, dramatic Nordic landscapes — Mandal offers a tournament setting that feels both powerful and peaceful at the same time.

At the heart of the event stands Martin Haven, whose dedication and energy have helped push Norwegian footvolley forward. Together with a fast-growing and passionate Norwegian footvolley community, Mandal 100 reflects years of steady development and belief in the sport.

Norway has been quietly building strength on the European stage — producing competitive players and a tight-knit community. Now, that momentum becomes visible on the League map.

The 25th of July Mandal 100 will be open, welcoming, and full of life. Expect a beautiful tournament both for men and women in stunning surroundings, high-level matches mixed with local energy, and good friends everywhere on and around the sand.

The League keeps expanding.
 New coastlines. New communities.

Mandal is ready.

title: Barcelona 500 Officially Announced
text:
From Circuit Catala 2025

Europe’s Biggest Footvolley Community Welcomes the League 2nd - 4th of April

The Barcelona 500 has officially been released — and it promises to be one of the defining stops of the season.

The sun is waiting.
The season is building.
The level is rising.

title: BIG names will compete in Amsterdam 500
text:
In Pula 2025: Jushua Lukas and Saeed Asiaban from Cologne Seals

The League of Champions season is officially underway, and all eyes are now turning to Amsterdam, where the Amsterdam 500 promises an explosive level of competition this March.

The entry list already makes one thing clear: This will be the strongest fields League of Champions has seen so far in a 500 tournament. All signs point to one thing: the League of Champions season is well and truly alive. With world-class teams, new duplas, and returning stars, Amsterdam 500 is shaping up to deliver a crazy-high level of footvolley this March.

We can’t wait.

title: Team Isli takes the gold – Stockholm 100 Sets the Bar for 2026
text:
Photo by: Murman Media

The 2026 League of Champions season kicked off in spectacular fashion this weekend with the inaugural Stockholm 100, marking the first-ever League of Champions tournament in Sweden. The event delivered exactly what fans had hoped for: elite-level footvolley, exciting new duplas, and an impressive standard worthy of a 100-category tournament.

From the opening matches, it was clear that the level was exceptionally high. Established top teams mixed with newly formed duplas, creating unpredictable matchups and an electric atmosphere throughout the tournament. The indoor facilities in Stockholm provided a perfect setting, allowing players to perform at their highest level and giving spectators a close-up experience of world-class footvolley.

The tournament title was claimed by Juan Silva, the Brazilian star now living in Portugal, together with Isli Bejtega – who were in top form. Representing Team Isli, the duo showed consistency, flair, and tactical maturity throughout the competition, ultimately lifting the trophy after a strong final performance.

Second place went to Joel Nisslein and Roman Uhr from Hertha Berlin, who once again proved why they are considered one of Europe’s most solid and well-organized clubs. The Hertha duo’s run to the final highlighted the growing depth and professionalism of European Club Footvolley.

One of the tournament’s most exciting storylines came from Bergen Footvolley, who reached the semifinals with, among others, Jonas Øvsthus. Øvsthus is regarded as one of Europe’s emerging talents, and his performance in Stockholm confirmed that he is very much a player to watch in the coming years.

Beyond the results, the Stockholm 100 was a celebration of the sport itself—bringing together the best established players and the next generation on the same court. The combination of elite competition, new partnerships, and top-tier organization made the event a landmark moment for the League of Champions.

With Stockholm setting a strong tone for the season, attention now turns to the next stop on the tour: Amsterdam 500 in March, where the stakes—and the spectacle—will be even higher.
